title: Cassoulet
subtitle: Slow-cooked French white bean and meat stew from the Languedoc
excerpt: The great dish of south-west France: white haricot beans slow-cooked with pork, sausages, and duck confit, buried under a golden breadcrumb crust that is broken and reformed multiple times during cooking. A project dish that rewards patience.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cassoulet is the defining dish of the Languedoc region of southern France, named for the cassole, the wide-mouthed earthenware dish in which it is traditionally cooked. The dish is the subject of fierce regional controversy: Castelnaudary claims to be the authentic source, while Carcassonne and Toulouse each insist on their own versions with different meats. The Castelnaudary version uses pork and duck confit; the Toulouse version adds Toulouse sausages; the Carcassonne version includes mutton. The common element is dried white beans — haricot or the traditional Tarbais — cooked with rich meats and a breadcrumb crust that is broken and reformed repeatedly during cooking. The dish takes its name from Prosper Montagné who described it as the God of Languedoc cookery.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, 3-litre earthenware or ovenproof casserole.
A large saucepan for cooking the beans.

content.text: Soak the dried beans overnight: they swell considerably and need to be fully cooked before the final baking stage, or they absorb all the liquid in the oven and become chalky. The breadcrumb crust is integral to the dish: traditionally broken and submerged into the stew seven times to absorb the fat, then reformed. In practice, breaking and pushing it down two or three times during the oven stage produces an excellent result.

items.preparation: dried; soaked overnight in cold water
or 2 duck legs confit from a tin
thick pork sausages, or Toulouse sausages if available
or lardons, in a single piece or cut into chunks

content.text: Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh cold water, and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour until tender but not collapsing. Drain, reserving the cooking water.

Brown the pork shoulder and sausages in batches in a little oil in a large pan over high heat. Remove. Cook the bacon in the same pan until the fat renders. Add the onion, carrot, and garlic and cook for 8 minutes. Add the tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, thyme, bay leaves, and 300 ml of the reserved bean water. Simmer for 10 minutes.

Heat the oven to 150 C (130 C fan). In a wide earthenware dish, layer the beans with the meat and the sauce, ending with a layer of beans. Press the duck legs into the top. Mix the breadcrumbs with the parsley and scatter over the top. Bake uncovered for 1.5 to 2 hours. After 45 minutes, push the crust down into the stew and re-scatter crumbs; repeat after another 30 minutes. The final crust should be deeply golden.
